notice: Reviewer-assigned relationships between reports. These are the labels V027/V028 matching is scored against. Relations never cross the development/holdout boundary.

duplicate_pairs.basis: Same asset, same subsystem and defect, observations 5 hours apart, coordinates within accuracy radius. Reported in different languages by different participants.

reviewer.notes: Two distinct participants corroborate one issue; participation count must be 2, evidence count 2.

duplicate_pairs.basis: Cross-language duplicate on a holdout asset: en-IN and mr-IN describing the same collapsed roof section.

reviewer.notes: Primary cross-language matching test for V046.

nearby_distinct.basis: A leaking roof and a broken window pane at the same school are separate defects with separate repairs. Proximity alone must not merge them.

reviewer.notes: Hard negative: identical location, different subsystem.

nearby_distinct.basis: A broken drinking-water tap and exposed wiring at the same school route to different departments.

reviewer.notes: Also a routing divergence case: same asset, two custodians.

nearby_distinct.basis: Collapsed roof section versus a broken window pane on the same holdout asset.

reviewer.notes: Hard negative for V046; a false merge here is the expensive error.

recurrence.basis: The same tap failed again three months after a confirmed repair.

reviewer.notes: V003 §8 requires that recurrence is not silently classified. Both treatments are defensible; the corpus records that a human must choose, and scoring must not penalise either choice.
